story_text.value:
With the team we are building a network management tool: switch upgrades, data collection/analytics, etc. With the write operations on production switches we've been requested to add an AAA flow so we have only 1 entry point for all microservices. For that reason we decided to add a proxy in the first place, so each request goes through the proxy, authenticates with External Authentication (the first A), then proceeds to the next step etc.

First we thought about squid/envoy, but these proxies were declined by our devops as planned for the future. For sure we found a workaround, but then I thought why there are almost no proxies with UI/ACLs/limits/quotas/speed limits etc.

So I decided to create my own solution that works out of the box with 1 simple command:

  docker run -d --name proxium -p 80:80 -p 8080:8080 -v proxium:/var/lib/proxium \
    -e SUPERUSER_CREATE=true -e SUPERUSER_EMAIL=admin@example.com \
    -e SUPERUSER_PASSWORD=change-me ikoldakov/proxium
Then open http://localhost, log in, create a proxy account and use it: curl -x http://username:password@localhost:8080 https://ifconfig.me curl -x socks5h://username:password@localhost:8080 https://ifconfig.me

Also, proxium supports https for the admin panel with self-signed certificates, let's encrypt certificates or your own uploaded ones. The proxy itself supports TLS too (self-signed, uploaded or imported from certbot).

External auth is not supported yet, but it's next in the roadmap: an HTTP hook in nginx auth_request style first, then JWTs from your identity provider. SSO over OIDC for the admin panel is planned as well.

I used AI for some parts of the code

Feedback is welcome!

title.value: Show HN: Proxium – Self-hosted HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy with a web admin UI

story_text.value:
I am involved in a community that acts as an accountability group.

So every morning, we have a daily meeting where we share our goals, what was planned and achieved yesterday, and today's agenda.

What I like the most is what sometimes happens after the daily meeting. We stay and have an open conversation about anything: entrepreneurship, the latest trendy product, personal subjects…

It feels like the genuine discussion that you can have when you are invited to someone's home or you are at a nice event (not the kind where there is networking).

Starting from this vision, I wanted to create the ingredients for that genuine discussion to happen: I've made a first version of Cliqqe.

A platform where you are matched with a group of 4 people to have a virtual dinner.

The first session is to happen tomorrow.

Happy to answer your questions and get your feedback. Also curious to know if the landing page conveys the vision or if it sounds more like "networking".

story_text.value:
Hello HN, I'm Leo, I built Minute of Fame as a weekend-size project, a joke that got out of hands.

Each day has 1440 minutes in it. Each one of them have an owner. When your minute comes around, your profile goes live on the dial for 60 seconds, and whoever is watching can react and wave. Then the next owner takes over. And so on.

Anyone can watch. Open minutes start at $5. If you want to buy a minute that already has an owner, you can offer a higher price.

Another thing that makes it different is that you can cash out - via Stripe Connect. So if your minute got bought at 2x, you can actually get the money.

Some interesting things I've found while building it:

* Time zones. Minutes are numbered in UTC, and displayed in user's local timezone. It might be slightly odd, but probably the best solution under the constrains

* An empty dial look bad, so we populated it with some messages to keep users entertained. Including some of my (lame) jokes

* There is a background music that is dynamically generated. It changes based on several things, including users reactions. It's an interesting problem to solve - make the music evolve but do not sound chaotic.

I launched it last night - would love some feedback.

title.value: Show HN: Minute of Fame – own one minute of the day, it airs live every day

story_text.value:
I am a Software engineer by trade. My main passion and love is music and songwriting, and sometimes I produce and release music.

I play a little guitar (over 35 years lol), and I have always dabbled in piano, never seriously enough until recently, when I decided I wanted to get somewhat better technically.

I also wanted to able to play nice chord progressions and be able to edit and tweak these progressions with a tool. That led me to building pianotry, more for myself and my daughter (who has started playing and plays by ear also and quite well).

I figure the best way to start is trying to play stuff that sounds good, and only go deeper if you want to, no sense letting the theory get in the way of the sound initially.

I also figured it would be cool to make a jsfiddle/codepen variant for piano progressions, which allows you to build and share your ideas.

I also have a next chord suggester for making progressions.

So this is my first pass at a little tool to do this.

I am trying to bake as much in as simply as I can.

I know there are many piano apps and sites out there, but this is just me building through my lens.

https://pianotry.com

title.value: Show HN: PianoTry, Play and remix beautiful chord progressions
